description:
## Problem
Two tests failed once each on unrelated PRs and passed on rerun:
- test_cancellation_kills_trapping_child_and_grandchild (UAT process-state, medium-test shard 3): assertion 'zombie' == 'gone', on develop run 43254948280 after PR #4173 (2026-11-12).
- tests/unit/utils/test_heavy_vm.py::test_the_real_stop_process_is_group_killed_with_its_output_kept_and_no_leaked_worker, first CI run of PR #4189 (2026-11-12).
ci-spurious-failures-under-runner-congestion-20261115 covers a different watchdog test and the duration gate. A test that accepts 'gone' but sees 'zombie' is likely asserting before the parent reaps the child.

## Decision gate
For each test, find whether the flake is a test timing assumption (assert before reap) or a product defect (cancellation leaves an unreaped child in real use). A product defect gets fixed in the product; a test-only race gets a deterministic wait on the condition (reap or exit), never a sleep or a retry decorator.

## Guardrails
- No xfail, skip, rerun-on-failure marker or widened assertion that would also accept a real leak.
- Prove determinism: run each test 200 times under load (pytest -n 8 with the medium shard) through make heavy-run with zero failures.
